ai.title: SDK: Dynamic esbuild import for compiled binaries
ai.summary: SDK agent loader now dynamically imports `esbuild` inside `transpileAgent` to support compiled binary environments. Static imports caused failures when `esbuild` was unavailable in bundled executables. The change is isolated to `sdk/src/agents/load-agents.ts`. If `esbuild` fails to load, local TypeScript agents are skipped with a verbose warning, while pre-bundled agents continue to function.

eli5.text: When you run the software as a packaged app on your computer, the tool that translates local custom assistants into a language your machine understands couldn't be found, causing those custom assistants to silently fail. We made the tool load only when needed instead of always, so the packaged app no longer breaks at startup. Today, if you run a packaged version and ask it to use a local custom assistant that needs translation, it will skip it with a notice instead of crashing. Pre-built assistants you download still work as before.

ai.title: Set absWorkingDir in esbuild to fix test isolation
ai.summary: Added `absWorkingDir: process.cwd()` to the esbuild configuration in `sdk/src/agents/load-agents.ts`. This forces esbuild to resolve paths relative to the current working directory, preventing test isolation issues caused by ambient directory state. The change ensures consistent transpilation behavior for agent loading within the SDK.

eli5.text: When the software loads a helper program to run in the background, it now makes sure to start that helper from the folder you're actually working in, instead of getting confused by leftover directory information from earlier steps. This prevents background testing checks from interfering with each other. If you watched the loading process happen, you would see it consistently start helpers from your current folder. This fix is in place and live today.

ai.title: CI: Upgrade actions to v4 and update runner targets
ai.summary: GitHub Actions `actions/checkout` and `actions/cache` upgraded from v3 to v4 across CI, evals, and nightly workflows. The `cli-release-build` workflow now targets `macos-13` instead of `macos-15-intel` for Darwin x64 builds. Internal knowledge base updated to reflect Bun v1.3.0 and new action versions.

eli5.text: The team updated the behind-the-scenes tools GitHub uses to run automated tests and build releases. For macOS releases, the build now runs on a slightly older macOS version (13) instead of the newer arm64 model (15); everything else continues to run as before. If you were watching the test logs or release jobs in GitHub, you'd see the macOS build job name change and slightly faster dependency loading, since the new action versions cache packages more efficiently.

ai.title: CLI 1.0.554 ships SDK esbuild import and CI actions v4
ai.summary: CLI package version bumped to 1.0.554 in cli/release/package.json, bundling the SDK's dynamic esbuild import in sdk/src/agents/load-agents.ts for compiled binary support and the GitHub Actions v4 upgrade across CI workflows. The SDK agent loader now dynamically imports esbuild inside transpileAgent, falling back to skipping local TypeScript agents with a verbose warning when esbuild is unavailable in bundled executables, while pre-bundled agents continue to function. CI workflows upgrade actions/checkout and actions/cache from v3 to v4 and switch the cli-release-build Darwin x64 target to macos-13.
ai.evidence: Modified file cli/release/package/ackage.json: version field changed from 1.0.553 to 1.0.554 (commit ddb306e2). Release ships SDK dynamic esbuild import in sdk/src/agents/load-agents.ts and CI actions v4 upgrade in .github/workflows.

eli5.text: This release makes the Freebuff command-line tool more reliable and up-to-date with modern developer tools. The SDK (software development kit) that loads AI agents now handles pre-built programs better, so custom TypeScript agents won't break when running inside compiled packages; if the code-translation tool is missing, those local agents are safely skipped while the built-in ones keep working. Path resolution during agent setup was also fixed, so tests and local runs behave consistently no matter which folder you start from. Behind the scenes, all automated build and testing steps were upgraded from GitHub Actions v3 to v4 (with newer checkout and cache tools), and the macOS build target was refreshed to support current Apple computers. Users benefit from fewer loading errors when using custom agents, faster and more consistent automated checks during updates, and continued compatibility with modern development environments.

ai.title: Update macOS runner labels in release workflows
ai.summary: Replaces macos-13 with macos-15-intel in CLI and npm app release build workflows. Ensures darwin-x64 binaries compile on current supported macOS runners. Affects .github/workflows/cli-release-build.yml and .github/workflows/npm-app-release-build.yml.

eli5.text: The build process that prepares your downloadable Mac software for release was switched from an older testing computer to a newer one. This only affects people who download the CLI tool or the npm desktop app on Intel-based Macs, and since version 1.0.554 is already released, this change takes effect for the next version. You wouldn't notice any difference at install time other than the release being built on a newer macOS version.

ai.title: CLI 1.0.555 bumps version and swaps to macos-15-intel runners
ai.summary: The CLI package version is bumped to 1.0.555 in cli/release/package.json, a release-metadata-only change. The user-visible update rolled into this release swaps macOS runner labels from macos-13 to macos-15-intel in the cli-release-build and npm-app-release-build workflows so darwin-x64 binaries compile on currently supported macOS runners. No functional code changes ship in this version; the bump gates the runner-label workflow update.
ai.evidence: The diff for cli/release/package.json changes the version field from 1.0.554 to 1.0.555. This is accompanied by the same-day commit sequence where the only other update in release 1.0.555 is the macOS runner label swap from macos-13 to macos-15-intel in .github/workflows/cli-release-build.yml and .github/workflows/npm-app-release-build.yml to compile darwin-x64 binaries on current supported macOS runners.

eli5.text: This release updates the CLI to version 1.0.555 and moves macOS software builds to newer Apple hardware running macOS 15, which keeps the Mac download compatible with current supported macOS systems. The change affects how the CLI and npm app are packaged and released, ensuring that the tools compile properly on up-to-date macOS runners (GitHub's build environment). Upgrading to this version means your Freebuff CLI and npm app will install and run without trouble on newer macOS machines, since the released binaries are now built using macOS 15 and Intel-based Mac hardware rather than the older macOS 13 environment.

ai.title: Fix local agent loading in compiled binaries
ai.summary: Local TypeScript agents now load correctly in compiled binaries where esbuild is unavailable. The `transpileAgent` function in `sdk/src/agents/load-agents.ts` adds a fallback to `Bun.build` if esbuild import fails or throws. This ensures agents defined in local files are transpiled and executed even when the standard Node.js build tools are missing from the runtime environment.

eli5.text: When you ask the program to run a helper script written in TypeScript (one of the languages it understands), it needs to translate that script into something the computer can run directly. If the usual tool for that translation is missing from your installed setup, the program now has a built-in backup translator so your helper script still runs instead of being skipped entirely. You'd notice because previously those scripts would silently do nothing in this situation, and now they actually run.

ai.title: Freebuff 1.0.556 ships local agent loading fix for compiled binaries
ai.summary: Version bumped to 1.0.556 in cli/release/package.json as a release tag. This release ships the prior fix where the transpileAgent function in sdk/src/agents/load-agents.ts now falls back to Bun.build when esbuild fails to load, ensuring local TypeScript agents load correctly in compiled binaries where esbuild is unavailable. Existing live sessions are unaffected; users gain reliable local agent loading in bundled executable environments.
ai.evidence: Version field updated from 1.0.555 to 1.0.556 in cli/release/package.json (diff shows single line change in the version field). Analysis notes confirm this is a release-bump commit shipping the local agent loading fix detailed in the release updates.

eli5.text: Local custom agents run reliably in the full standalone application. When you add your own AI helpers stored as local files, they now load and work correctly even when the program is run as a compiled, installed app where certain internal build tools are missing. This means your custom agent files will be prepared and run without errors regardless of how Freebuff was installed on your computer. Upgrading makes your local agent workflows more dependable, so you won't hit failures just because a helper component isn't present in the runtime environment.

ai.title: Consolidate error utilities and reduce verbose API error logs
ai.summary: The CLI imports getErrorObject from @codebuff/common/util/error, deleting cli/src/utils/error.ts. getErrorObject now accepts includeRawError option and extracts status/code fields. Agent runtime simplifies APICallError messages to just error.message, removing URL, headers, and body dumps. OpenRouter stream handlers use structured logging with includeRawError: true.

eli5.text: When the assistant hit an error talking to an AI provider, the logs would dump a huge wall of technical detail including the full request URL, headers, and response body. Now the logs just show the actual error message, so troubleshooting is easier and quieter. Behind the scenes, the code that shapes those error messages was merged into one shared spot and gained the ability to optionally include the raw error detail when developers specifically ask for it, which some streaming connections do.

ai.title: Make CLI usage banner clickable
ai.summary: Usage banner text is now a clickable Button opening WEBSITE_URL + '/usage' via open(). BottomBanner layout refactored to render close button outside text/children block, allowing custom children to fill space. generateUsageBannerText appends '. See more' to indicate interactivity. Scope: cli/src/components/bottom-banner.tsx, cli/src/components/usage-banner.tsx, cli/src/utils/usage-banner-state.ts.

eli5.text: When you use the command-line tool, the small status bar at the bottom of your screen that shows your usage or credits now has a clickable link at the end of its text. Instead of just displaying text like 'You have 120 credits used. See more', you can actually click on the message itself to open a detailed usage page in your web browser. Behind the scenes, this was done by treating the entire banner text as a tappable button, separate from the existing close button, so that clicking anywhere in the message (not just the 'x') takes you straight to the full usage breakdown. This makes it easier to find out exactly where your allowance is going without having to manually navigate to the website.
